If all level maps of T' are Fredholm with the same index, then ker T'_m = ker T'_0 and F_m/R_m = F_0/R_0 by a dimension count (dim ker drops, codim rises because F_m is dense, indices agree), so T' is regularizing. A regularizing sc-operator with Fredholm level maps is sc-Fredholm: this is the project's construction for Prop. 1.10, copied with its bootstrap replaced (regularizing_of_index, isScFredholm_of_regularizing). B_to_A uses B only for the level conjunct (T+S sc-Fredholm, then IsScFredholm.fredholmIndex_lvl). The index equality ind(T+S) = ind T, which is A's actual extra content and absent from the text, comes from the classical compact-perturbation theorem fredholmIndex_add_isCompactOperator, without B. So both directions compile, but in content A is strictly stronger: B plus Kato's index theorem gives A. That is why the relation is A_stronger even though B_to_A is formally proved.
